+ A good teaching interface should preserve orientation. The learner + should be able to see where a lesson is going, understand which ideas + depend on which others, inspect a diagram at a useful scale, and + recover from a failed model turn without reconstructing the question. + Keating 2.6 treats those as parts of the same problem: keeping the path + through a subject legible. +

+ +

Provider-owned access

+

+ Keating's hosted-model option now uses Not Organic instead of the + legacy Dio and Bifrost implementation. Identity, wallet balance, + checkout, usage records, and DPoP capabilities remain account-scoped + and provider-owned. The browser no longer receives or recovers a + virtual provider key; Keating's same-origin routes exchange the + active product session for narrowly scoped model access on the server. +

+

+ Pricing and settings now describe that relationship directly. Credit + packs top up one shared wallet, another device can resume through the + same Not Organic identity, and bringing an independent provider key + remains available for learners who prefer it. +

+ +

Nested learning paths

+

+ Study plans are no longer flat checklists. A plan can contain several + substantial coverage areas, each with nested concepts or activities, + expected outcomes, time estimates, and resumable progress. Stable + identifiers connect prerequisites across the hierarchy, and Keating + derives the dependency graph from those relationships rather than + asking the model to describe the same structure twice. +

+

+ The OpenUI operating prompt now includes canonical interactive-question + and detailed-plan programs that are validated against the live + component grammar. This gives the model a concrete example of when to + ask through the structured interface and what a useful multi-area + lesson plan looks like. +

+ +

Expandable diagrams

+

+ Every shared Mermaid surface can now expand into a full-viewport + inspector. Wide maps remain scrollable at their natural scale instead + of shrinking into illegibility. The inspector closes by button, + backdrop, or Escape and returns keyboard focus to the control that + opened it. Nested study-plan dependencies use this same renderer, so + the graph can begin as a compact disclosure and grow when the learner + needs to trace it. +

+ +

Retry without rewriting

+

+ Keating already knew how to remove a trailing failed response and + replay the preceding prompt, but the action was easy to miss. Failed + turns now end with an accessible recovery alert and a primary + Retry prompt action. The recovery reuses the original + learner turn and existing session state; it does not ask the learner + to copy, edit, or remember what was lost. +

+ +

Verification

+

+ The release was checked through the full web test suite, TypeScript + validation, Vite and Nitro production builds, Storybook's static + build, generated NodePod prompt snapshots, and rendered browser passes + for retry recovery, nested plans, dependency disclosure, diagram + expansion, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration. +

+ A good teaching interface should preserve orientation. The learner + should be able to see where a lesson is going, understand which ideas + depend on which others, inspect a diagram at a useful scale, and + recover from a failed model turn without reconstructing the question. + Keating 2.6 treats those as parts of the same problem: keeping the path + through a subject legible. +

+ +

Provider-owned access

+

+ Keating's hosted-model option now uses Not Organic instead of the + legacy Dio and Bifrost implementation. Identity, wallet balance, + checkout, usage records, and DPoP capabilities remain account-scoped + and provider-owned. The browser no longer receives or recovers a + virtual provider key; Keating's same-origin routes exchange the + active product session for narrowly scoped model access on the server. +

+

+ Pricing and settings now describe that relationship directly. Credit + packs top up one shared wallet, another device can resume through the + same Not Organic identity, and bringing an independent provider key + remains available for learners who prefer it. +

+ +

Nested learning paths

+

+ Study plans are no longer flat checklists. A plan can contain several + substantial coverage areas, each with nested concepts or activities, + expected outcomes, time estimates, and resumable progress. Stable + identifiers connect prerequisites across the hierarchy, and Keating + derives the dependency graph from those relationships rather than + asking the model to describe the same structure twice. +

+

+ The OpenUI operating prompt now includes canonical interactive-question + and detailed-plan programs that are validated against the live + component grammar. This gives the model a concrete example of when to + ask through the structured interface and what a useful multi-area + lesson plan looks like. +

+ +

Expandable diagrams

+

+ Every shared Mermaid surface can now expand into a full-viewport + inspector. Wide maps remain scrollable at their natural scale instead + of shrinking into illegibility. The inspector closes by button, + backdrop, or Escape and returns keyboard focus to the control that + opened it. Nested study-plan dependencies use this same renderer, so + the graph can begin as a compact disclosure and grow when the learner + needs to trace it. +

+ +

Retry without rewriting

+

+ Keating already knew how to remove a trailing failed response and + replay the preceding prompt, but the action was easy to miss. Failed + turns now end with an accessible recovery alert and a primary + Retry prompt action. The recovery reuses the original + learner turn and existing session state; it does not ask the learner + to copy, edit, or remember what was lost. +

+ +

Verification

+

+ The release was checked through the full web test suite, TypeScript + validation, Vite and Nitro production builds, Storybook's static + build, generated NodePod prompt snapshots, and rendered browser passes + for retry recovery, nested plans, dependency disclosure, diagram + expansion, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration. +

content.text:
Released Keating `v2.6.0`.

- Published [GitHub release v2.6.0](https://github.com/Diogenesoftoronto/keating/releases/tag/v2.6.0) with Linux x64, macOS x64, and macOS arm64 bundles.
- Pushed commit `56e56c9` and annotated tag to `main`; local and remote match with a clean worktree.
- Updated the [release blog](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/pages/Blog.tsx:264) and [changelog](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/CHANGELOG.md:8). The `2.6.0` blog bundle is already live on keating.help.
- Fixed the stale Pi entrypoint check in the release workflow. All three CI bundles built, verified, and uploaded successfully.
- Passed root tests, 477 web tests, 44 mobile tests, typechecks, production builds, Storybook, package verification, and version checks.

The only remaining failure is npm publication: npm rejected the configured Actions credential with `E404` during `PUT keating@2.6.0`. The GitHub release and downloadable bundles are unaffected.
